## Bundled alert rules[​](#bundled-alert-rules "Direct link to Bundled alert rules")

9 rules. Each lists its trigger condition (PromQL) and the steps to take when it fires. Thresholds are meant to be adjusted after import.

### HighgRPCResourceExhaustedRate[​](#highgrpcresourceexhaustedrate "Direct link to HighgRPCResourceExhaustedRate")

High gRPC ResourceExhausted error rate

S2 Warning · for 60 min · Trigger:

```
sum without (grpc_code, grpc_method, grpc_service, grpc_type) (

  rate(grpc_server_handled_total{grpc_code="ResourceExhausted"}[5m])

) / sum without (grpc_code, grpc_method, grpc_service, grpc_type) (

  rate(grpc_server_handled_total[5m])

) * 100 > 1
```

Runbook:

1. On the Gitaly node, check the logs to see which RPCs are being limited (gitaly\_concurrency\_limiting related);
2. Use gitlab-ctl status plus node CPU/IO to confirm Gitaly is overloaded;
3. Determine whether an oversized repository or a misbehaving client is pulling repeatedly, and throttle that source temporarily;
4. If capacity is genuinely short, raise Gitaly's concurrency limits and add nodes.

### HighPumaUtilization[​](#highpumautilization "Direct link to HighPumaUtilization")

Puma instance {{ $labels.instance }} has more than 90% thread utilization ({{ $value | printf "%.1f" }}%) over the last 60 minutes.

S2 Warning · for 60 min · Trigger:

```
instance:puma_utilization:ratio * 100 > 90
```

Runbook:

1. On the GitLab node run gitlab-ctl status to check the puma process and look for timeouts in /var/log/gitlab/puma/;
2. Combine with the PumaQueueing alert to judge the queue depth;
3. Short term, raise puma\['worker\_processes'] and max\_threads then run gitlab-ctl reconfigure;
4. Look for slow requests (large MR diffs, big repository pages) holding workers for a long time and rate limit them if needed.

### PostgresDatabaseDeadlocks[​](#postgresdatabasedeadlocks "Direct link to PostgresDatabaseDeadlocks")

Postgres database has deadlocks

S2 Warning · Trigger:

```
increase(pg_stat_database_deadlocks[5m]) > 0
```

Runbook:

1. On PostgreSQL confirm log\_lock\_waits=on and take the full SQL of both deadlock participants from the log;
2. Join pg\_locks with pg\_stat\_activity to identify which two tables are waiting on each other;
3. In GitLab this commonly comes from CI concurrently updating the same records — reduce concurrency or upgrade GitLab (upstream frequently fixes these);
4. Check whether a long transaction is amplifying the deadlock probability.

### PostgresDown[​](#postgresdown "Direct link to PostgresDown")

The Postgres service {{ $labels.job }} instance {{ $labels.instance }} is not responding for more than 50% of the time for 5 minutes.

S2 Warning · Trigger:

```
avg_over_time(pg_up[5m]) * 100 < 50
```

Runbook:

1. Log in to the PostgreSQL node and confirm the process is alive (gitlab-ctl status postgresql or systemctl status postgresql);
2. If it is alive, connect by hand with psql to tell a hung instance from a network or pg\_hba problem;
3. If it is not running, read the tail of the PG log (full disk, full WAL directory, OOM) before starting it;
4. If a standby exists, assess whether to fail over.

### PumaQueueing[​](#pumaqueueing "Direct link to PumaQueueing")

Puma instance {{ $labels.instance }} is queueing requests with an average of {{ $value | printf "%.1f" }} over the last 30 minutes.

S2 Warning · Trigger:

```
avg_over_time(puma_queued_connections[30m]) > 1
```

Runbook:

1. Combine with HighPumaUtilization to confirm worker utilization;
2. Check /var/log/gitlab/puma/puma\_stdout.log and the gitlab-rails log for the slowest request paths;
3. Short term, raise puma\['worker\_processes'] and run gitlab-ctl reconfigure;
4. Longer term, find the root cause of the slow requests (large repositories, large MRs, unindexed queries) and add nodes if needed.

### RedisDown[​](#redisdown "Direct link to RedisDown")

The Redis service {{ $labels.job }} instance {{ $labels.instance }} is not responding for more than 50% of the time for 5 minutes.

S2 Warning · Trigger:

```
avg_over_time(redis_up[5m]) * 100 < 50
```

Runbook:

1. Log in to the Redis node and check the process with gitlab-ctl status redis or systemctl status redis;
2. If it is alive, verify with redis-cli ping to tell a hang from a network or password problem;
3. If it is not running, check the logs (OOM, or a full disk breaking the RDB write) before starting it;
4. After recovery, check whether the Sidekiq queues are backed up and watch them drain.

### ServiceDown[​](#servicedown "Direct link to ServiceDown")

The service {{ $labels.job }} instance {{ $labels.instance }} is not responding for more than 50% of the time for 5 minutes.

S2 Warning · Trigger:

```
avg_over_time(up[5m]) * 100 < 50
```

Runbook:

1. Take job/instance from the alert labels to identify the component (gitaly/puma/sidekiq/registry, etc.);
2. On that node run gitlab-ctl status to check the process state;
3. Use gitlab-ctl tail \<service> to find the exit reason in the logs;
4. After restarting, run gitlab-rake gitlab:check for an overall health check.

### SidekiqJobsQueuing[​](#sidekiqjobsqueuing "Direct link to SidekiqJobsQueuing")

Sidekiq has jobs queued

S2 Warning · for 60 min · Trigger:

```
sum by (name) (sidekiq_queue_size) > 0
```

Runbook:

1. Take name from the alert labels to identify the backed-up queue;
2. Check queue depth and failed jobs in the GitLab admin Background Jobs page or via gitlab-rails runner;
3. Confirm the Sidekiq process is alive and that concurrency is not set too low (sidekiq\['max\_concurrency']);
4. If it is caused by mass job failures and retries, find the failure root cause (Redis/PG problems, external timeouts) before clearing them.

### WorkhorseHighErrorRate[​](#workhorsehigherrorrate "Direct link to WorkhorseHighErrorRate")

Workhorse has high error rates

S2 Warning · Trigger:

```
(

  sum without (job, code) (

    job_route_method_code:gitlab_workhorse_http_request_duration_seconds_count:rate5m{code=~"5.."}

  ) /

  sum without (job,code) (

    job_route_method_code:gitlab_workhorse_http_request_duration_seconds_count:rate5m

  ) < 10

) * 100 > 50
```

Runbook:

1. Run gitlab-ctl tail gitlab-workhorse to see the exact errors and the failing routes;
2. The usual root cause is a puma timeout or Gitaly being unavailable — confirm both are healthy first;
3. For large-file issues, check disk space and temporary directory permissions;
4. If it lines up with a recent upgrade, roll back first.

# Monitor HAProxy with Nightingale

Reads HAProxy's CSV stats page or Runtime API for sessions, queues, errors and health state per frontend, backend and server.

Last reviewed 2026-10-31

The HAProxy input reads the CSV output of the stats page (`/stats;csv`) or the Runtime API Unix socket. It collects current and maximum sessions, queue length, request rate, status code classes, connection and response errors, retries and redispatches at frontend, backend and server level, plus the health-check result of every backend server. Verified against real backend traffic.

The rules cover backend servers marked DOWN, backends with no servers left, queue buildup, rising 5xx and HAProxy itself being unreachable.

## What's in the template[​](#whats-in-the-template "Direct link to What's in the template")

* **1 dashboard**, 10 panels in total
* **8 alert rules**, each with runbook steps
* **Categraf collector config**: `input.haproxy`

## How to connect[​](#how-to-connect "Direct link to How to connect")

1. [Install Categraf](https://n9e.github.io/docs/data/categraf/install.md), put the config below in `conf/input.haproxy/haproxy.toml`, fill in your own address and credentials, and restart Categraf. The startup log prints `input: local.haproxy started` once the plugin is loaded.

   ```
   [[instances]]

   # URI on which to scrape HAProxy.

   # e.g. 

   # uri = "http://localhost:5000/baz?stats;csv"

   # uri = "http://user:pass@haproxy.example.com/haproxy?stats;csv"

   # uri = "unix:/run/haproxy/admin.sock"

   uri = ""



   # Flag that enables SSL certificate verification for the scrape URI

   ssl_verify = false



   # Comma-separated list of exported server metrics. See http://cbonte.github.io/haproxy-dconv/configuration-1.5.html#9.1

   server_metric_fields = ""



   # Comma-separated list of exported server states to exclude. See https://cbonte.github.io/haproxy-dconv/1.8/management.html#9.1, field 17 status

   server_exclude_states = ""



   # Timeout for trying to get stats from HAProxy.

   timeout = "5s"



   # Flag that enables using HTTP proxy settings from environment variables ($http_proxy, $https_proxy, $no_proxy)

   proxy_from_env = false
   ```

2. Open the integration center in Nightingale, find HAProxy, and [import the dashboards and alert rules](https://n9e.github.io/docs/data/integrations/import.md) into a business group.

3. Imported rules start disabled. [Check that the metrics are arriving](https://n9e.github.io/docs/data/integrations/verify.md) first, then enable the rules one by one with thresholds that fit your environment.

## Bundled dashboards[​](#bundled-dashboards "Direct link to Bundled dashboards")

| Dashboard           | Panels |
| ------------------- | ------ |
| HAProxy By Categraf | 10     |

## Bundled alert rules[​](#bundled-alert-rules "Direct link to Bundled alert rules")

8 rules. Each lists its trigger condition (PromQL) and the steps to take when it fires. Thresholds are meant to be adjusted after import.

### HAProxy instance unreachable[​](#haproxy-instance-unreachable "Direct link to HAProxy instance unreachable")

S1 Critical · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
haproxy_up == 0
```

Runbook:

1. Log in to the host and run systemctl status haproxy to confirm the process is alive;
2. If it is alive, verify the stats endpoint by hand with curl -s http\://\<host>:\<port>/stats;csv and check whether an ACL or firewall is blocking it;
3. If it is not running, validate the config first with haproxy -c -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg, then start it and check /var/log/haproxy.log for the exit reason;
4. Confirm the VIP layer (keepalived or similar) has failed over, otherwise move traffic to the standby node by hand.

### HAProxy backend entirely unavailable[​](#haproxy-backend-entirely-unavailable "Direct link to HAProxy backend entirely unavailable")

S1 Critical · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
haproxy_backend_up == 0
```

Runbook:

1. Take the backend name from the alert labels and run echo 'show stat' | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy.sock to see the state and down reason of every server in that backend;
2. curl each backend address from the HAProxy host to tell a collective backend failure apart from a HAProxy-to-backend network problem;
3. If the backends are healthy, check whether the backend's check configuration (probe path, timeout, rise/fall) is too aggressive;
4. If it cannot be recovered quickly, switch traffic to a standby backend or a degraded page.

### HAProxy backend server unavailable[​](#haproxy-backend-server-unavailable "Direct link to HAProxy backend server unavailable")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
haproxy_server_up == 0
```

Runbook:

1. Take backend and server from the alert labels and log in to that backend host to confirm the application process and port are alive;
2. curl the backend address from the HAProxy host to tell an application failure apart from a network problem;
3. For an application failure, follow that application's own recovery procedure, then confirm HAProxy has automatically added it back (haproxy\_server\_up returns to 1);
4. Run echo 'show stat' | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy.sock to see how many servers are still available in the backend, and scale out immediately if headroom is low.

### HAProxy backend 5xx ratio too high[​](#haproxy-backend-5xx-ratio-too-high "Direct link to HAProxy backend 5xx ratio too high")

S1 Critical · for 3 min · Trigger:

```
sum by (backend) (rate(haproxy_backend_http_responses_total{code="5xx"}[5m])) / sum by (backend) (rate(haproxy_backend_http_responses_total[5m])) > 0.05
```

Runbook:

1. Take the backend name from the alert labels and first determine whether every server is erroring or only one (compare haproxy\_server\_http\_responses\_total{code="5xx"});
2. If it is one server, remove it from the backend to stop the bleeding;
3. If all of them are erroring, check the backend application logs for the root cause (dependency timeouts, exhausted connection pool, a bug from a release);
4. If it lines up with a recent release, roll back first rather than keep investigating.

### HAProxy backend requests queueing[​](#haproxy-backend-requests-queueing "Direct link to HAProxy backend requests queueing")

S2 Warning · for 5 min · Trigger:

```
haproxy_backend_current_queue > 0
```

Runbook:

1. Take the backend name from the alert labels and compare with haproxy\_backend\_http\_response\_time\_average\_seconds to tell a slower backend apart from rising concurrency;
2. If the backend got slower, investigate on the application side (slow queries, GC, dependency timeouts);
3. If concurrency rose, check whether maxconn on the backend and its servers is set too low, raise it and reload;
4. If backend capacity is genuinely insufficient, add more servers.

### HAProxy frontend sessions approaching the limit[​](#haproxy-frontend-sessions-approaching-the-limit "Direct link to HAProxy frontend sessions approaching the limit")

S2 Warning · for 5 min · Trigger:

```
haproxy_frontend_limit_sessions > 0 and haproxy_frontend_current_sessions / haproxy_frontend_limit_sessions > 0.8
```

Runbook:

1. Take the frontend name from the alert labels and determine whether this is natural traffic growth or abnormal traffic (slow connections, crawlers);
2. For natural growth, raise the frontend maxconn and the global maxconn, confirm the system ulimit -n and memory are sufficient, then reload;
3. For abnormal traffic, add a stick-table rate limit on the frontend or block the source IPs outright;
4. Check whether many connections are sitting idle for a long time and tighten timeout client.

### HAProxy backend response time too high[​](#haproxy-backend-response-time-too-high "Direct link to HAProxy backend response time too high")

S2 Warning · for 5 min · Trigger:

```
haproxy_backend_http_response_time_average_seconds > 1
```

Runbook:

1. Take the backend name from the alert labels and compare haproxy\_backend\_http\_connect\_time\_average\_seconds with http\_queue\_time\_average\_seconds to tell slow connects, long queueing and slow backend processing apart;
2. For long queueing, handle it as request queueing (raise maxconn or scale out);
3. For slow processing, investigate on the application side (slow queries, GC, downstream timeouts);
4. You may raise timeout server temporarily so requests are not cut off while you investigate, but do not treat it as a long-term fix.

### HAProxy backend connection errors[​](#haproxy-backend-connection-errors "Direct link to HAProxy backend connection errors")

S2 Warning · for 3 min · Trigger:

```
increase(haproxy_backend_connection_errors_total[5m]) > 0
```

Runbook:

1. Take the backend name from the alert labels and run echo 'show stat' | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy.sock to see which server's connection errors are growing;
2. telnet or curl that backend address from the HAProxy host to tell a closed port, a refused connection and a connect timeout apart;
3. If the backend process is healthy, check the network in between, the security groups, and whether the backend's backlog/somaxconn is saturated;
4. Check whether the backend's timeout connect is set too short and causing false positives.

# Monitor Huawei Cloud with Nightingale

Scrape Cloud Eye (CES) metrics converted to Prometheus format by the cloudeye-exporter; templates cover ECS, RDS, DCS, ELB, Kafka, RocketMQ, CSS and WAF.

Last reviewed 2026-10-31

Huawei Cloud metrics come from the Cloud Eye service (CES). The `cloudeye-exporter` maintained by Huawei Cloud converts CES metrics per product namespace into Prometheus metrics named `huaweicloud_sys_<service>_<metric>`, which the Categraf `prometheus` input scrapes.

The templates are split by product: ECS hosts, RDS (MySQL and PostgreSQL), DCS Redis instances and proxy nodes, ELB, distributed messaging (Kafka, RabbitMQ, RocketMQ), Cloud Search (CSS/ES) and WAF, one dashboard each. The rules cover ECS CPU and memory, RDS connections and disk, DCS memory and hit ratio, ELB backend health; the metric reference explains each product's metrics one by one.

## What's in the template[​](#whats-in-the-template "Direct link to What's in the template")

* **14 dashboards**, 330 panels in total
* **35 alert rules**, each with runbook steps
* **286 metric descriptions**

## How to connect[​](#how-to-connect "Direct link to How to connect")

Deploy the [cloudeye-exporter](https://github.com/huaweicloud/cloudeye-exporter) and configure it with an IAM account's AK/SK, the project and the namespaces to collect. Once `http://<exporter>:8087/metrics?services=SYS.ECS` responds, scrape it per namespace with the Categraf `prometheus` input:

```
# conf/input.prometheus/huaweicloud.toml

interval = 120



[[instances]]

urls = ["http://<exporter>:8087/metrics?services=SYS.ECS,SYS.RDS,SYS.DCS,SYS.ELB"]

labels = { job = "huaweicloud" }
```

Cloud Eye metrics are at 60-second granularity or coarser, so do not collect more often than that.

1. Open the integration center in Nightingale, find Huawei Cloud, and [import the dashboards and alert rules](https://n9e.github.io/docs/data/integrations/import.md) into a business group.
2. Imported rules start disabled. [Check that the metrics are arriving](https://n9e.github.io/docs/data/integrations/verify.md) first, then enable the rules one by one with thresholds that fit your environment.

## Bundled alert rules[​](#bundled-alert-rules "Direct link to Bundled alert rules")

35 rules. Each lists its trigger condition (PromQL) and the steps to take when it fires. Thresholds are meant to be adjusted after import.

### Huawei Cloud ECS CPU usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-cpu-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS CPU usage exceeds 80%")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_cpu_usage >80
```

Runbook:

1. SSH in and use top -H to find the busiest processes and threads;
2. Use perf top or a language profiler to find the hot functions;
3. Tell business growth apart from a code fault (infinite loop, frequent GC);
4. For growth, change to a larger flavour in the console or scale out horizontally.

### Huawei Cloud ECS inode usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-inode-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS inode usage exceeds 80%")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_SlAsH_disk_inodesUsedPercent >80
```

Runbook:

1. Run df -i to find the mount point;
2. Count files level by level to find the directories with the most small files;
3. Common sources are log fragments, session files and container layers — confirm and bulk delete;
4. Longer term, consider moving small-file workloads to a dedicated partition.

### Huawei Cloud ECS NTP offset exceeds 1 second[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-ntp-offset-exceeds-1-second "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS NTP offset exceeds 1 second")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_ntp_offset > 1000
```

Runbook:

1. Run chronyc tracking to check the offset and upstream source state;
2. Huawei Cloud ECS should use the internal NTP service (ntp.myhuaweicloud.com) — confirm it is configured;
3. Start chronyd if it is not running and enable it at boot;
4. For a large offset, use chronyc makestep to step the clock.

### Huawei Cloud ECS TIME\_WAIT connections exceed 20000[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-time_wait-connections-exceed-20000 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS TIME_WAIT connections exceed 20000")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_net_tcp_close > 20000
```

Runbook:

1. Run ss -s to see the real connection state distribution;
2. Run ss -tan | awk '{print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn to find the peers;
3. The root cause is usually too many short-lived connections — switch the application to long-lived connections or a pool;
4. As an emergency measure enable net.ipv4.tcp\_tw\_reuse and widen ip\_local\_port\_range.

### Huawei Cloud ECS zombie processes above 0[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-zombie-processes-above-0 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS zombie processes above 0")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_proc_zombie_count >0
```

Runbook:

1. Run ps -ef | awk '$2 \~ /Z/ || $8 \~ /Z/' or ps aux | grep 'Z' to find the zombie processes and their parent PPIDs;
2. Once you have the parent, the problem is that it never calls wait() — this must be fixed in code;
3. As an emergency measure restart the parent so init reaps the zombies;
4. If the count keeps growing, the code fix is mandatory — restarting is only a stopgap.

### Huawei Cloud ECS available memory below 20%[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-available-memory-below-20 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS available memory below 20%")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_mem_available < 20
```

Runbook:

1. Run free -h to check available memory and swap;
2. Run ps aux --sort=-%mem | head to find the largest consumer and judge whether it is leaking;
3. For a leak, capture a heap in the application — a restart alone is not enough;
4. For growth, change to a larger memory flavour in the console.

### Huawei Cloud ECS outbound packet loss rate exceeds 50%[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-outbound-packet-loss-rate-exceeds-50 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS outbound packet loss rate exceeds 50%")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_net_dropout > 50
```

Runbook:

1. Run ip -s link show to confirm TX dropped is growing;
2. Confirm whether the instance flavour's bandwidth cap is saturated — cloud bandwidth is capped per flavour and exceeding it drops packets;
3. If capped, adjust bandwidth or change the flavour in the console;
4. If not capped, check security groups, the kernel transmit queue and the application's send logic.

### Huawei Cloud ECS outbound packet error rate exceeds 50%[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-outbound-packet-error-rate-exceeds-50 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS outbound packet error rate exceeds 50%")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_net_errout > 50
```

Runbook:

1. Run ip -s link show and ethtool -S to confirm the error counters;
2. In the cloud the physical layer is the provider's responsibility, so an abnormal error rate should go to a Huawei Cloud support ticket first;
3. At the same time confirm whether the instance flavour's bandwidth cap was exceeded;
4. If redundancy exists, move traffic away to stop the impact.

### Huawei Cloud ECS block device usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-block-device-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS block device usage exceeds 80%")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_SlAsH_disk_usedPercent > 80
```

Runbook:

1. Run df -h to find the mount point and du -x --max-depth=1 for the largest directories;
2. Clean logs and temporary files first, and use lsof +L1 for deleted-but-unreleased files;
3. Expand the EVS disk online in the console, then use growpart plus resize2fs/xfs\_growfs to grow the filesystem;
4. Longer term, evaluate moving the data directory to a dedicated cloud disk.

### Huawei Cloud ECS inbound packet loss rate exceeds 50%[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-inbound-packet-loss-rate-exceeds-50 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS inbound packet loss rate exceeds 50%")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_net_dropin > 50
```

Runbook:

1. Run ip -s link show to confirm RX dropped is growing;
2. Confirm whether the instance flavour's bandwidth or PPS cap is saturated — cloud instances limit both;
3. If capped, adjust bandwidth or change the flavour in the console;
4. If not capped, raise the receive ring buffer with ethtool -G and consider enabling RPS.

### Huawei Cloud ECS inbound packet error rate exceeds 50%[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-inbound-packet-error-rate-exceeds-50 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS inbound packet error rate exceeds 50%")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_net_errin > 50
```

Runbook:

1. Run ip -s link show and ethtool -S to confirm the error counters;
2. In the cloud the physical layer is the provider's responsibility, so an abnormal error rate should go to a Huawei Cloud support ticket first;
3. At the same time confirm whether the flavour's bandwidth/PPS cap was exceeded;
4. If redundancy exists, move traffic away.

### Huawei Cloud ECS disk write IOPS too high[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-disk-write-iops-too-high "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS disk write IOPS too high")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_SlAsH_disk_agt_write_requests_rate > 99
```

Runbook:

1. Run iostat -x 1 to check actual IOPS and await;
2. Run iotop -oP to find the process writing the most;
3. Compare against the EVS disk type's IOPS ceiling to see whether it has topped out — ultra-high performance and general purpose disks differ greatly;
4. If it has, upgrade the disk type or expand it in the console (IOPS usually scales linearly with capacity); if not, optimise the application's write pattern.

### Huawei Cloud ECS disk read IOPS too high[​](#huawei-cloud-ecs-disk-read-iops-too-high "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ECS disk read IOPS too high")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_agt_SlAsH_disk_agt_read_requests_rate > 99
```

Runbook:

1. Run iostat -x 1 to check actual IOPS and await;
2. Run iotop -oP to find the process reading the most;
3. Compare against the EVS disk type's IOPS ceiling to see whether it has topped out;
4. If it has, upgrade the disk type or expand it; if not, reduce disk reads with caching and better indexes.

### Huawei Cloud ELB L4 inbound bandwidth usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-elb-l4-inbound-bandwidth-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ELB L4 inbound bandwidth usage exceeds 80%")

S2 Warning · for 2 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_elb_l4_in_bps_usage > 80
```

Runbook:

1. Check that ELB's bandwidth monitoring curve in the console to tell sustained growth from a spike;
2. Determine whether it is normal business growth or abnormal traffic (crawlers, attacks);
3. For genuine growth, adjust the ELB specification or bandwidth cap in the console;
4. For abnormal traffic, use WAF/DDoS protection to rate limit or block.

### Huawei Cloud ELB L4 outbound bandwidth usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-elb-l4-outbound-bandwidth-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ELB L4 outbound bandwidth usage exceeds 80%")

### Huawei Cloud ELB L4 concurrent connection usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-elb-l4-concurrent-connection-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud ELB L4 concurrent connection usage exceeds 80%")

```
huaweicloud_sys_elb_l4_con_usage > 80
```

Runbook:

1. Check that ELB's connection count monitoring in the console for the growth trend;
2. Check whether the backend is responding more slowly and causing connections to pile up — a high connection count is often a symptom of a slow backend rather than the cause;
3. If the backend is fine, upgrade the ELB specification for the growth;
4. Check whether clients are failing to reuse connections.

### Huawei Cloud Redis average CPU usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-average-cpu-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis average CPU usage exceeds 80%")

This metric samples the CPU usage of the measured object multiple times within the statistics period and reports the average. Only single-node/primary-standby/read-write-splitting instances are supported.

S2 Warning · for 2 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_cpu_avg_usage > 80
```

Runbook:

1. Run SLOWLOG GET 10 to find the slowest commands;
2. Focus on O(N) commands such as KEYS, HGETALL and SMEMBERS and on big-key operations, switching to SCAN or batching;
3. Check whether an RDB/AOF persistence run is causing the CPU spike;
4. If it stays high after tuning, upgrade the instance flavour in the console.

### Huawei Cloud Redis memory usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-memory-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis memory usage exceeds 80%")

S1 Critical · for 2 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_memory_usage > 80
```

Runbook:

1. Use redis-cli --bigkeys to find large keys and split them or add TTLs;
2. Use INFO memory to check the fragmentation ratio and enable activedefrag if it is high;
3. Check whether keys without an expiry keep accumulating;
4. Confirm maxmemory-policy, then expand the flavour in the console.

### Huawei Cloud Redis slow log detected[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-slow-log-detected "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis slow log detected")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_is_slow_log_exist == 1
```

Runbook:

1. Run SLOWLOG GET 10 for the specific slow commands and their timings;
2. Focus on O(N) commands and big-key operations;
3. Switching to SCAN with batching and splitting large keys is the real fix;
4. If the slow commands come from a scheduled job, move it to off-peak hours.

### Huawei Cloud Redis bandwidth usage exceeds 90%[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-bandwidth-usage-exceeds-90 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis bandwidth usage exceeds 90%")

This metric samples the CPU usage of the measured object multiple times within the statistics period and reports the average. Only single-node/primary-standby/read-write-splitting instances are supported.

S2 Warning · for 2 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_bandwidth_usage > 90
```

Runbook:

1. Use INFO stats to check instantaneous\_input\_kbps / output\_kbps and determine the direction;
2. Use redis-cli --bigkeys to find large keys — reading and writing large keys is the most common cause of saturated bandwidth;
3. Split large keys and reduce one-shot bulk reads;
4. If you genuinely need more bandwidth, upgrade the flavour in the console.

### Huawei Cloud Redis new connections exceed 10000[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-new-connections-exceed-10000 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis new connections exceed 10000")

For single-node and primary-standby instances the connection limit is 10000; adjust the threshold to your workload.

S3 Info · for 2 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_total_connections_received > 10000
```

Runbook:

1. Use CLIENT LIST grouped by source to find the clients reconnecting frequently;
2. Switching the application to a connection pool with reused connections is the real fix;
3. Check whether the client's connection timeout is set too short and causing repeated reconnects;
4. Confirm no throttling or memory alarm is causing the server to close connections.

### Huawei Cloud Redis max CPU usage exceeds 80%[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-max-cpu-usage-exceeds-80 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis max CPU usage exceeds 80%")

S2 Warning · for 2 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_cpu_usage > 80
```

Runbook:

1. Identify the node with high CPU in the console;
2. In cluster mode this is usually data skew — a hot key in one slot, findable with --hotkeys;
3. Hot keys can be mitigated with a local cache or by splitting the key;
4. If it stays high after rebalancing, upgrade the flavour.

### Huawei Cloud Redis active clients exceed 8000[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-active-clients-exceed-8000 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis active clients exceed 8000")

For single-node and primary-standby instances the connection limit is 10000; adjust the threshold to your workload.

S2 Warning · for 2 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_connected_clients > 8000
```

Runbook:

1. Check that DCS instance's monitoring curves in the Huawei Cloud console;
2. Connect with redis-cli and run INFO to confirm the real state of the relevant metric;
3. Once the cause is identified, follow the usual Redis path (big keys, slow commands, connection leaks);
4. If capacity is short, change the instance flavour in the console.

### Huawei Cloud Redis flow control count above 0[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-flow-control-count-above-0 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis flow control count above 0")

Check spec limits together with instantaneous inbound/outbound traffic to decide whether scaling up resolves it. Only Redis 4.0+ instances support this metric; Redis 3.0 instances do not.

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_rx_controlled > 0
```

Runbook:

1. Check when the throttling occurred in the console and compare against the bandwidth and QPS curves to see which limit was exceeded;
2. For bandwidth, use --bigkeys to find and split large keys;
3. For QPS, add a local cache or batch requests on the application side;
4. If you genuinely need more capacity, change the instance flavour in the console.

### Huawei Cloud Redis Proxy node active clients exceed 20000[​](#huawei-cloud-redis-proxy-node-active-clients-exceed-20000 "Direct link to Huawei Cloud Redis Proxy node active clients exceed 20000")

For single-node and primary-standby instances the connection limit is 10000; adjust the threshold to your workload.

S2 Warning · for 2 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dcs_p_connected_clients > 20000
```

Runbook:

1. Check that DCS instance's monitoring curves in the Huawei Cloud console;

### RocketMQ broker down[​](#rocketmq-broker-down "Direct link to RocketMQ broker down")

S1 Critical · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dms_broker_alive == 0
```

Runbook:

1. Confirm the instance and broker state in the Huawei Cloud console;
2. Confirm clients have failed over to other brokers — with multiple brokers only some partitions are unavailable;
3. If the console looks fine but clients report errors, check the network and security groups plus the client's nameserver address;
4. If it stays unavailable, open a ticket with Huawei Cloud.

### RocketMQ per-core CPU load exceeds 1.5[​](#rocketmq-per-core-cpu-load-exceeds-15 "Direct link to RocketMQ per-core CPU load exceeds 1.5")

S1 Critical · for 3 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dms_broker_cpu_core_load > 1.5
```

Runbook:

1. Check that broker's TPS and message backlog curves in the console to tell producer-side from consumer-side pressure;
2. For a heavy consume backlog, scale out consumers first;
3. For a produce spike, evaluate upgrading the instance flavour;
4. Confirm no oversized messages or huge batch sends are overwhelming the broker.

### RocketMQ memory usage exceeds 85%[​](#rocketmq-memory-usage-exceeds-85 "Direct link to RocketMQ memory usage exceeds 85%")

S1 Critical · for 3 min · Trigger:

```
huaweicloud_sys_dms_broker_memory_usage > 85
```

Runbook:

1. Check the message backlog in the console — a backlog consumes significant memory;
2. Restoring consumption to drain the backlog is the most direct fix;
3. Check whether the message retention period is set too long;
4. For sustained growth, upgrade the instance flavour.

## Metric reference[​](#metric-reference "Direct link to Metric reference")

286 metrics, the ones the dashboards and rules above are built on.

| Metric                                                      | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Unit    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_auth_errors`                           | Authentication Failures — Counts the number of authentication failures on the instance. Only single-node and master/standby instances are supported.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_blocked_clients`                       | Blocked Clients — This metric measures the number of clients suspended by blocking operations, such as BLPOP, BRPOP, and BRPOPLPUSH.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_client_biggest_in_buf`                 | Biggest Client Input Buffer — This metric measures the maximum input data length among all current client connections.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | bytes   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_client_longest_out_list`               | Longest Client Output List — This metric measures the longest output list among all current client connections.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_command_max_delay`                     | Maximum Command Latency — Measures the maximum command latency of the instance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | ms      |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_connected_clients`                     | Connected Clients — This metric counts the number of connected clients, including connections for system monitoring, configuration synchronization, and service traffic.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_cpu_usage`                             | Maximum CPU Usage — This metric samples the CPU usage of the monitored object multiple times within the statistics period and reports the highest sampled value. For single-node and master/standby instances, this metric is the CPU usage of the master node. For Proxy Cluster instances, this metric is the average value across all proxy nodes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | %       |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_evicted_keys`                          | Evicted Keys — This metric counts the number of keys deleted due to insufficient memory during the period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_expired_keys`                          | Expired Keys — This metric counts the number of keys deleted due to expiration during the period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_instantaneous_input_kbps`              | Instantaneous Network Input Traffic — This metric measures the instantaneous input traffic.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | bit/s   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_instantaneous_ops`                     | Ops per Second — This metric counts the number of commands processed per second.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_instantaneous_output_kbps`             | Instantaneous Network Output Traffic — This metric measures the instantaneous output traffic.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | bit/s   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_is_slow_log_exist`                     | Slow Log Existence — Indicates whether slow logs exist on the instance. Slow logs caused by the migrate, slaveof, config, bgsave, and bgrewriteaof commands are not counted. Only single-node and master/standby instances are supported.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_keys`                                  | Total Keys — This metric counts the total number of keys in the Redis cache. Only single-node and master/standby instances are supported.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_keyspace_hits`                         | Keyspace Hits — This metric counts the number of successful lookups in the main dictionary during the period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_keyspace_hits_perc`                    | Cache Hit Ratio — This metric measures the cache hit ratio of Redis, calculated as: keyspace\_hits/(keyspace\_hits+keyspace\_misses)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | %       |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_keyspace_misses`                       | Keyspace Misses — This metric counts the number of failed lookups in the main dictionary during the period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_memory_frag_ratio`                     | Memory Fragmentation Ratio — This metric measures the current memory fragmentation ratio, which equals used\_memory\_rss / used\_memory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_memory_usage`                          | Memory Usage — This metric measures the memory usage of the monitored object (reserved memory is excluded from the calculation).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | %       |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_net_in_throughput`                     | Network Input Throughput — This metric measures the average inbound traffic per second on the network port.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | bytes/s |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_net_out_throughput`                    | Network Output Throughput — This metric measures the average outbound traffic per second on the network port.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | bytes/s |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_pubsub_channels`                       | Pub/Sub Channels — This metric counts the number of Pub/Sub channels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_pubsub_patterns`                       | Pub/Sub Patterns — This metric counts the number of Pub/Sub patterns.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_rejected_connections`                  | Rejected Connections — This metric counts the number of connections rejected during the period because the maxclients limit was exceeded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_total_commands_processed`              | Commands Processed — This metric counts the number of commands processed during the period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_total_connections_received`            | New Connections — This metric counts the number of connections created during the period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_total_net_input_bytes`                 | Network Input Bytes — This metric counts the number of bytes received during the period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | bytes   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_total_net_output_bytes`                | Network Output Bytes — This metric counts the number of bytes sent during the period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | bytes   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_used_memory`                           | Used Memory — This metric measures the number of bytes of memory used by Redis.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | bytes   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_used_memory_lua`                       | Used Memory (Lua) — This metric measures the number of memory bytes used by the Lua engine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | bytes   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_used_memory_peak`                      | Used Memory Peak — This metric measures the peak memory usage of Redis since the server started.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | bytes   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_used_memory_rss`                       | Used Memory RSS — This metric measures the RSS memory used by Redis, that is, the amount of memory actually resident in RAM, including heap memory but excluding swapped-out memory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | bytes   |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_command_avg_rt`                        | Average Latency — Average latency from when the node receives a command to when it sends a response.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | μs      |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_command_max_rt`                        | Maximum Latency — Maximum latency from when the node receives a command to when it sends a response.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | μs      |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_command_p99_rt`                        | P99 Latency — 99th percentile of command execution latency.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | ms      |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_connected_clients`                     | Connected Clients — Number of connected clients, including connections for system monitoring, configuration synchronization, and services.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |         |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_connections_usage`                     | Connection Usage — Percentage of the current number of connections to the maximum number of connections allowed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | %       |
| `huaweicloud_sys_dcs_cpu_avg_usage`                         | Average CPU Usage — The CPU usage of the monitored object is sampled multiple times within each monitoring period. This metric indicates the average of the sampled values.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | %       |

| `huaweicloud_sys_agt_SlAsH_disk_agt_read_bytes_rate`        | (Agent) Disk Read Rate — This metric measures the volume of data read from the monitored object per second. # Monitor IPMI with Nightingale

Reads out-of-band temperature, fan, voltage, power and sensor state over IPMI, from the local BMC or remote ones.

Last reviewed 2026-10-31

The IPMI input is ported from ipmi\_exporter. It runs a set of FreeIPMI commands and turns the output into metrics: temperatures, fan speeds, voltages, power draw, the health of every sensor and the chassis power state. The data comes from the BMC, so it is still available when the operating system is down.

Collect locally on each server, or point one collector at a list of remote BMC addresses and credentials. IPMI itself must already be configured so that commands such as `ipmimonitoring` return output; otherwise there is nothing to convert.

## What's in the template[​](#whats-in-the-template "Direct link to What's in the template")

* **3 dashboards**, 31 panels in total
* **4 alert rules**, each with runbook steps
* **19 metric descriptions**
* **Categraf collector config**: `input.ipmi`

## How to connect[​](#how-to-connect "Direct link to How to connect")

1. [Install Categraf](https://n9e.github.io/docs/data/categraf/install.md), put the config below in `conf/input.ipmi/conf.toml`, fill in your own address and credentials, and restart Categraf. The startup log prints `input: local.ipmi started` once the plugin is loaded.

   ```
   # Read metrics from the bare metal servers via freeipmi

   [[instances]]

   # target指定是本地采集还是远程采集

   #target="localhost"

   # 指定采集的用户名和密码，这里务必保证ipmi命令能获取正确输出，不是网上查到一个用户名 密码就可以。

   #user = "user"

   #pass = "1234"



   # ipmi协议版本，支持1.5 和 2.0

   #driver = "LAN_2_0"



   # 指定特权用户名

   #privilege = "user"



   ## session-timeout, ms

   #timeout = 100000



   # 支持的采集器  bmc, bmc-watchdog, ipmi, chassis, dcmi, sel，sm-lan-mode

   # 默认使用 bmc, ipmi, chassis和dcmi，建议保持下列配置便于仪表盘更好的展示

   collectors = [ "bmc", "ipmi", "chassis", "sel", "dcmi"]



   # 不关注的传感器，指定id 排除掉

   #exclude_sensor_ids = [ 2, 29, 32, 50, 52, 55 ]



   # 如果你想使用定制化的参数覆盖内置的命令，可以修改以下内容； 建议保持注释

   #[instances.collector_cmd]

   #ipmi = "sudo"

   #sel = "sudo"

   #[instances.default_args]

   #ipmi = [ "--bridge-sensors" ]

   #[instances.custom_args]

   #ipmi = [ "--bridge-sensors" ]

   #sel = [ "ipmi-sel" ]
   ```

2. Open the integration center in Nightingale, find IPMI, and [import the dashboards and alert rules](https://n9e.github.io/docs/data/integrations/import.md) into a business group.

3. Imported rules start disabled. [Check that the metrics are arriving](https://n9e.github.io/docs/data/integrations/verify.md) first, then enable the rules one by one with thresholds that fit your environment.

| Dashboard           | Panels |
| ------------------- | ------ |
| IPMI                | 12     |
| IPMI by Categraf    | 12     |
| IPMI for Prometheus | 7      |

## Bundled alert rules[​](#bundled-alert-rules "Direct link to Bundled alert rules")

4 rules. Each lists its trigger condition (PromQL) and the steps to take when it fires. Thresholds are meant to be adjusted after import.

### CPU temperature exceeds 90[​](#cpu-temperature-exceeds-90 "Direct link to CPU temperature exceeds 90")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
ipmi_cpu1_temp{} > 90 or ipmi_cpu2_temp{} > 90
```

Runbook:

1. Run ipmitool sdr type temperature to see the actual readings and thresholds of each temperature sensor;
2. Check that all chassis fans are spinning (ipmitool sdr type fan) and that filters and heatsinks are not clogged with dust;
3. Confirm the room air conditioning and cold aisle temperature are normal and whether other machines in the same rack are also hot;
4. Short term, reduce load on this machine or move critical workloads off to buy time for a dust-clean or fan replacement.

### Abnormal CPU voltage[​](#abnormal-cpu-voltage "Direct link to Abnormal CPU voltage")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
count by (agent_hostname, server) ({__name__=~"ipmi_vcpu[0-9]+", status_code=~"lcr|ucr"}) > 0
```

Runbook:

1. Run ipmitool sdr type voltage to see each voltage sensor's reading against its upper and lower thresholds and which way it deviates;
2. Check the power supply status (ipmitool sdr type 'Power Supply'); on dual-PSU machines confirm whether one feed has failed;
3. Check the power line and PDU output stability, and whether other machines in the same rack are alarming at the same time;
4. If a PSU is confirmed faulty, schedule a replacement and move critical workloads off meanwhile.

### Abnormal fan speed[​](#abnormal-fan-speed "Direct link to Abnormal fan speed")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
count by (agent_hostname, server) ({__name__=~"ipmi_fan[0-9]+", status_code=~"lcr|lnc|unc|ucr"}) > 0
```

Runbook:

1. Run ipmitool sdr type fan to see each fan's speed and thresholds and identify the faulty one;
2. A fan reading 0 or far below its peers is almost certainly failed — schedule a replacement;
3. If every fan is running fast, intake temperature or load is too high: check room temperature, dust in the filters and any airflow obstruction;
4. Before swapping fans, run ipmitool sdr type temperature to see whether temperatures have already risen, and move workloads off if needed.

### Motherboard temperature exceeds 90[​](#motherboard-temperature-exceeds-90 "Direct link to Motherboard temperature exceeds 90")

S2 Warning · for 1 min · Trigger:

```
ipmi_system_temp > 90 or ipmi_pch_temp > 90
```

Runbook:

1. Run ipmitool sdr type temperature to identify which sensor is hot and what its threshold is;
2. Check the chassis fans and airflow, especially whether cabling is blocking intake around the motherboard;
3. Confirm the room air conditioning and in-rack temperature, and whether the machine is wedged into an enclosed spot;
4. Clean the dust, tidy the cabling and re-measure; if it still does not drop, contact the vendor to inspect the heatsink assembly.
